Bumigat ang trapiko sa magkabilang lanes ng EDSA dahil sa kasagsagan ng Friday rush hour kahapon, Disyembre 5.

Ang naranasang mabigat na daloy ng trapiko ay pinalala ng maraming insidente ng banggaan at tumirik na mga sasakyan.

Nakapagtala ang Metropolitan Manila Development Authority (MMDA) ng 23 road crash incidents at walong stalled vehicles mula 2pm hanggang 9pm. Ang insidenteng ito ay pawang naasistehan ng mga traffic enforcers ng ahensiya.

Batay sa traffic monitoring, nakapagtala ng heavy traffic sa EDSA northbound mula Guadalupe hanggang Megamall at EDSA southbound mula Dario Bridge hanggang Quezon City Academy (QCA) u-turn slot. Lumuwag naman ang sitwasyon ng trapiko sa ibang bahagi ng EDSA bandang alas-otso kagabi.

Nakatutok ang deployment ng mga traffic enforcers ng MMDA sa mga choke points at intersections sa mga pangunahing kalsada sa Metro Manila. #mmda

✈️Safety Update: Three In-Flight Malfunctions Resolved Safely, Airlines Launch Inspections

São Paulo, Brazil — At 14:20 local time on December 4, LATAM Airlines flight LA345 (São Paulo → Rio de Janeiro) experienced an incident while loading cargo on the ground, when a cargo conveyor caught fire and flames spread to the underside of the aircraft. The crew immediately initiated emergency procedures, evacuating 178 passengers via emergency slides. Only two passengers sustained minor abrasions and received medical attention. Airport fire crews extinguished the flames within 15 minutes. Preliminary findings indicate an electrical malfunction in the loading equipment, and LATAM has launched comprehensive inspections of all equipment of the same model.

Tokyo Narita Airport, Japan — At 22:10 on December 3, All Nippon Airways flight NH819 (Narita → Manila) experienced abnormal noise and mild vibration from its left engine approximately 30 minutes after takeoff. The crew shut down the affected engine and requested an emergency diversion to Tokyo Haneda Airport. The aircraft touched down safely at 23:05, and all 156 passengers were unharmed. ANA announced that it will conduct a teardown inspection of the engine together with Pratt & Whitney, and subsequent flights on the route will temporarily be operated by Boeing 777 aircraft.

Moscow Sheremetyevo Airport, Russia — At 23:40 on the same day, Red Wings Airlines flight WZ321 (Moscow → Phuket) detected a fire warning signal from its right engine about one hour after departure. Following standard emergency procedures, the crew returned to Moscow and landed safely at 01:10. All 212 passengers and 10 crew members evacuated safely. The cause of the incident remains under investigation.
#NEWS #Airlines #Aviation #WeeklyReview
